articles.headline: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years as private company
articles.summary: Chiltern Railways, which runs trains from London Marylebone to Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire, Warwickshire and the West Midlands, has returned to the public sector, ending three decades as a privately run company. It was privatised in 1996. It is the tenth rail company to be brought under Great British Railways (GBR), the government's plan to take passenger rail into public hands, which the government says will save money and improve services.
keywords: Business objectives: profit versus service to the public
Costs and benefits of state ownership, including government failure
Capacity and overcrowding as a service quality problem

articles.headline: Tata Steel seeks new government funding as industry crisis deepens
articles.summary: Tata Steel, the largest steel producer in the UK, has approached the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Technology to discuss a fresh multimillion-pound support package. Industry sources suggest the sum could reach hundreds of millions of pounds, though the exact figure is unclear.
keywords: Subsidies and the rightward shift of the supply curve
Government intervention to protect jobs and strategic industries
Government failure (information gaps, unintended consequences, cost of intervention)
Import competition and its effect on domestic producers

articles.headline: Thames Water rescue deal should be rejected - MPs
articles.summary: A cross-party committee of MPs has urged the government to reject a £10bn takeover proposal from Thames Water's creditors. Thames Water, the UK's biggest water company, serves 16 million customers and owes roughly £20bn.
keywords: Natural monopoly and regulation of monopoly power
Government intervention: fines, regulation and nationalisation
Government failure and the cost of intervention
Debt, creditors and the risk of business failure

articles.headline: Interest rates held but Bank signals rise if energy prices stay high
articles.summary: The Bank of England has left its main interest rate at 3.75% for the sixth time in a row, but its governor, Andrew Bailey, said energy price volatility makes a future rise more likely. The war involving Iran has disrupted global energy supplies, causing sharp increases in petrol and diesel prices.
keywords: Inflation target and the Monetary Policy Committee
Transmission of interest rate changes to spending and investment
Bond yields and the cost of government borrowing

articles.headline: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar
articles.summary: The UK's annual inflation rate rose to 3.1% in August, up from 2.9% in July and the first reading above 3% since March. The result matched what economists had expected.
keywords: Cost-push inflation and a shift left of short-run aggregate supply
External shocks and a net importer of energy

articles.headline: Inflation is outpacing wage growth again, squeezing Americans' paychecks
articles.summary: Prices in the US are rising faster than wages again. Consumer prices were 3.4% higher in August than a year earlier, while average hourly earnings rose only 3.1%. Adjusted for inflation, average hourly earnings fell 0.1% from July and 0.3% from a year earlier, so workers are losing purchasing power.
keywords: Consumption as a component of aggregate demand
Income elasticity of demand and inferior goods

articles.headline: Canada's retaliatory tariffs worth CA$27.6 billion take effect as trade rift with U.S. deepens
articles.summary: Canada has placed tariffs of between 15% and 50% on hundreds of US products worth CA$27.6 billion, with the measures taking effect on Tuesday. They cover goods such as dairy, agricultural equipment, paper, household appliances and electronics, and tariffs on US steel, aluminium and iron products doubled to 50%. Existing Canadian tariffs, including 25% on cars, remain in place.
keywords: Tariffs as a restriction on free trade
Effects of tariffs on consumers, producers and government revenue
Protectionism and the arguments for it

articles.headline: South Korea's semiconductor exports just tripled year-over-year. Is it too much of a good thing?
articles.summary: South Korea's chip exports have pushed overall exports to record levels. Semiconductor exports jumped 209% from a year earlier to $46.65 billion in August, accounting for 47.5% of total goods exports of $98.25 billion. The trade ministry said the increase was mainly caused by demand for AI infrastructure, as large cloud providers such as Google and Amazon increased their spending.
keywords: Exports as a component of aggregate demand (net trade)
Risks of over-specialisation and the case for diversification
Demand for exports depends on demand in other countries
Interest rates and the central bank's role in supporting growth
